Each verified before push: behind=0, zero conflict markers on the committed
tree, inventory --check rc=0. My script refused to auto-resolve anything outside
the inventory doc, which is why #2006 stopped rather than guessing.

#2006, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT NEEDED JUDGEMENT:

A semantic conflict in mailbox_cmd.rs, two hunks. main warns and starts a new
thread on an unresolved --in-reply-to and carries BUG-1231's short-id fallback;
the branch refuses and routes both through a new resolve_mailbox_thread().

I took the BRANCH side, but only after checking it SUBSUMES main rather than
discarding it. resolve_mailbox_thread does both of BUG-1231's resolutions —
`any(|m| m.thread_id == query)` for full ids, resolve_mailbox_message(..)
.thread_id for short ones — and then refuses instead of silently using an
unresolved id. So BUG-1231's capability survives; what changes is the failure
mode, which is BUG-1297's whole point. Taking main's side would have reverted
the tightening. Taking the branch's side WITHOUT checking would have risked
dropping BUG-1231 silently. I verified the two resolution lines are present in
the merged file rather than trusting the function name.

Second gap: BUG-1231 also added `subject: Option<String>` to Message and
MailboxCommand::Send, and three fixtures here predate it, so the crate did not
compile post-rebase. `subject: None` at each — the serde default.

    aida-cli-lib --lib   5203 passed, 0 failed

IF YOU DISAGREE WITH THE CONFLICT CALL, it is one commit to flip and I would
rather you look than take it. It is the only decision in the six that was not
mechanical.

SEPARATELY — #1998's F2 IS CLOSED AND CI-VERIFIED: step 25 Monitor contract
drift guard now SUCCESS, Build fully green, 32 success / 1 skipped. That is the
monitor-contract commit doing exactly what it was for. F1 stands and needs a
commit, not a rebase.

NOT TOUCHING: #2042 (held, live findings, TASK-1289 blocked on the operator),
#2043 (closed), #1989 (yours to route — it has a live F1 too).
